summary: Follow-up plan for layer Z.5 (vector bundles and curves) of 'Explicit K₀: projectives, rank and determinant'. The layer was planned by KTheoryLowDegrees--Z.3.json against the pinned libraries. Since then TauCetiRoadmap has merged AlgebraicVectorBundles and SchemeAndStackFoundations, which own finite locally free sheaves, exterior powers, determinants, K₀ and G₀ of a scheme, the determinant on K₀, the K/G comparison, degrees on curves and the affine Picard comparison. Tau Ceti main now also has the Picard group law and Cl ≅ Pic on regular curves. This packet rebases Z.5 on those suppliers through a routing map for the 40 earlier nodes, and adds two nodes. The first is an ample family of divisor line bundles on every regular noetherian curve, possibly non-separated, which gives the resolution property without Stacks 0F8A or the higher K-theory roadmap. The second is the exact degree comparison the roadmap's handoff contract asks for: on a proper regular curve over k, χ = rank·χ(O_X) + deg ∘ det on K₀, χ of a codimension-one point class is its residue degree. In dimension one, (rank, deg ∘ det) has image ℤ ⊕ δℤ with δ the index; for Spec K its image is ℤ × {0}. The main theorem K₀(X) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(X), the class formulas and the Dedekind and doubled-line cases stay in KTheoryLowDegrees--Z.3.json, read through the substitution table.

nodes.title: Regular curves carry an ample family of divisor line bundles
nodes.statement: Let X satisfy the regular-curve package. (a) For every nonempty open U ⊆ X the complement X ∖ U is a finite set of closed points, each of coheight one, so each is a codimension-one point of X. (b) The boundary divisor D_U := Σ_{z ∉ U} z in SchemeWeilDivisor X has coefficient 1 at the codimension-one points outside U and 0 at those of U, so it is effective; the divisor sheaf O_X(D_U) is invertible; the rational function 1 is a global section s_U of O_X(D_U); and s_U generates the stalk of O_X(D_U) exactly at the points of U, so its non-vanishing locus X_{s_U} equals U. (c) If U_1, …, U_m are nonempty affine opens covering X, the invertible sheaves O_X(D_{U_i}) with the sections s_{U_i} form an ample family of invertible modules on X in the sense of Stacks 0FXR (with exponent one). No separatedness or affine-diagonal hypothesis is used. A noetherian scheme all of whose local rings are regular of dimension ≤ 1 is a finite disjoint union of such schemes and of spectra of fields, and inherits an ample family componentwise (extend each sheaf by O and each section by 0 off its component). This is the input from which KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/regular-curve-resolution-property obtains the resolution property in the sense of SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.7 (Chow.HasResolutionProperty).
hypotheses: The regular-curve package of KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/regular-curve-integral: X is a noetherian integral scheme (IsNoetherian X, IsIntegral X) with coheight x ≤ 1 for every point x, whose local rings at codimension-one points are discrete valuation rings. No separatedness is assumed.
In (c) the opens U_i are affine; (a) and (b) hold for every nonempty open U.
If X has dimension zero it is Spec of a field, U = X, D_U = 0 and s_U = 1; the statements are then trivial.
proofSteps: (a) X is irreducible, so the nonempty open U contains the generic point η. Let z ∉ U. Then z ≠ η and η specializes to z, so coheight z ≥ 1, hence coheight z = 1 by hypothesis. A codimension-one point of a scheme all of whose points have coheight ≤ 1 is closed (Tau Ceti's isClosed_singleton_of_forall_coheight_le_one_of_coheight_eq_one). X ∖ U is closed in the noetherian space X, so it has finitely many irreducible components; each is the closure of a point of X ∖ U, which is closed, so each component is a single point and X ∖ U is finite.

(b) D_U is the finite sum of WeilDivisor.ofPoint z over the points z of (a), viewed in CodimensionOnePoint X; its coefficients are as stated (WeilDivisor.coeff of ofPoint). Every Weil divisor on X is locally principal (Tau Ceti's SchemeWeilDivisor.isLocallyPrincipal_of_forall_coheight_le_one), so SchemeWeilDivisor.sheaf D_U is invertible (SchemeWeilDivisor.toInvertibleSheaf). Its sections over an open V are the rational functions f with ord_z f ≥ −D_U(z) at every codimension-one z ∈ V; as D_U ≥ 0, f = 1 is a global section.

(b, continued) On U the coefficient of D_U vanishes, so O_X(D_U)|_U is O_U (SchemeWeilDivisor.unitIsoSheafZero restricted to U) and s_U = 1 generates every stalk there. At z ∉ U the stalk of O_X(D_U) is π_z^{−1}O_{X,z} for a uniformizer π_z of the discrete valuation ring O_{X,z}, and 1 = π_z·π_z^{−1} lies in the maximal ideal times the generator, so it does not generate. Hence X_{s_U} = U.

(c) Every point of X lies in some U_i = X_{s_{U_i}}, which is affine: this is Stacks 0FXR with n = 1. In dimension one the complement of a nonempty open is automatically the support of an effective Cartier divisor by (a)–(b); in general Stacks 0GML needs regularity together with an affine diagonal to reach the same conclusion, which is why separatedness never enters here.

How the family is used (Stacks 0GMM, made explicit by Stacks 01PW): for a coherent F, F|_{U_i} is generated by finitely many sections t_ij because U_i is affine and F is of finite type; X is noetherian, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so by Stacks 01PW each s_{U_i}^n t_ij extends for n ≫ 0 to a global section of F ⊗ O_X(n D_{U_i}), i.e. to a map O_X(−n D_{U_i}) → F whose image on U_i contains t_ij. The finitely many maps give a surjection from a finite direct sum of invertible sheaves onto F.

Disconnected case: by KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/regular-curve-integral a noetherian scheme with regular local rings of dimension ≤ 1 is a finite disjoint union of schemes satisfying the package and of spectra of fields; on a component Spec K take (O, 1). Extending each sheaf by O and each section by 0 off its component keeps X_s equal to the chosen affine open.
acceptance: X = P¹_k and U = P¹ ∖ {∞}: D_U = ∞, O_X(D_U) ≅ O(1), and s_U is the section of O(1) vanishing exactly at ∞.
X = Spec O_F for a number field F: for U = X, D_U = 0 and s_U = 1; for U = X ∖ {𝔭}, D_U = 𝔭 and O_X(D_U) is the fractional ideal sheaf 𝔭^{−1}.

X the affine line over k with doubled origin (KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/doubled-line-example), with charts U′, U″: D_{U′} = 0″ and D_{U″} = 0′, and {O(0″), O(0′)} is an ample family; this is the example of Stacks 0FXT, whose sections of L_1 and L_{−1} have the two charts as non-vanishing loci. X has no ample invertible sheaf, since a scheme with one is separated (Stacks 01PY); one line bundle cannot replace the family.

The hypothesis dim ≤ 1 cannot be dropped: on the affine plane with doubled origin the complement of either chart is a closed point of codimension two, which supports no Cartier divisor, and that scheme lacks the resolution property (SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.7 Check resolutionProperty_doubled_plane_rejected).

sources.match: Defines an ample family of invertible modules on a quasi-compact scheme: every point lies in an affine non-vanishing locus of a section of a tensor power of one of the sheaves. Part (c) verifies this with exponent one.
A quasi-compact regular scheme with affine diagonal has an ample family. Part (c) is the dimension-one case, where the affine-diagonal hypothesis is replaced by the finiteness of (a).
An ample family of invertible modules gives the resolution property; this is how KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/regular-curve-resolution-property uses (c).

On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, a section of a quasi-coherent module over the non-vanishing locus of a section s of an invertible sheaf is, after multiplying by a power of s, the restriction of a global section of the twisted module; used in the last proof step.

The affine line with zero doubled (Schemes, Example 26.14.3, tag 01JD, with n = 1) carries invertible sheaves trivial on both charts whose sections have the charts as non-vanishing loci, so it has an ample family of invertible modules although it is not separated; this is the doubled-line acceptance of (c).
A scheme with an ample invertible module is separated; so the doubled line has no ample invertible sheaf and needs a family.

nodes.title: Euler characteristic and degree on K₀ of a proper regular curve

planet.name: Euler characteristic and degree on K₀ of a curve

nodes.statement: Let k be a field and X a connected regular noetherian scheme of dimension ≤ 1, proper over k, with structure morphism f : X → Spec k (so X satisfies the regular-curve package and is separated). Write K₀(X) = Chow.K0 X and G₀(X) = Chow.G0 X (SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.7), c_X = Chow.K0.toG0 X, which is bijective by KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/regular-curve-cartan-iso, and χ_k := f_! ∘ c_X : K₀(X) → G₀(Spec k) ≅ ℤ, where f_! is the K-theoretic pushforward of §5.7, [F] ↦ Σ_i (−1)^i [R^i f_* F], so that χ_k[E] = Σ_i (−1)^i dim_k H^i(X, E). Let deg_k : Pic(X) → ℤ be the degree deg_k L = χ(X, L) − χ(X, O_X) (Stacks 0AYR; §3.3's vectorBundleDegree in rank one), on Pic(X) = LineBundleClass X. Then: (a) for every x ∈ K₀(X), χ_k(x) = rank(x)·χ(X, O_X) + deg_k(det x), with rank and det the homomorphisms of KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/curve-rank-determinant-equivalence; in particular deg_k is a group homomorphism. (b) For a closed codimension-one point y, χ_k(c_X⁻¹[κ(y)_y]) = [κ(y) : k] = deg_k O_X(y); for a Weil divisor D = Σ_y n_y y, χ_k(cl[D]) = deg_k(det cl[D]) = deg_k O_X(D) = Σ_y n_y [κ(y) : k], which is Tau Ceti's SchemeWeilDivisor.relativeDegree f D; here cl is the point-class map of KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/point-class-map. (c) If dim X = 1, the map (rank, deg_k ∘ det) : K₀(X) → ℤ² has image ℤ ⊕ δ_X ℤ, where δ_X is the greatest common divisor of the residue degrees [κ(y) : k] of the closed points (the index of X); it is onto exactly when δ_X = 1, for instance when X has a k-rational point. Degrees are weighted by residue degrees: counting closed points gives a different and wrong answer as soon as some [κ(y) : k] > 1. If dim X = 0, then X = Spec K for a finite extension K/k, Pic(X) = 0, and the image of (rank, deg_k ∘ det) is ℤ × {0}; the closed point of Spec K has codimension zero and is not a Weil-divisor generator.
hypotheses: k a field; X connected, regular, noetherian, of dimension ≤ 1 and proper over k (hence separated and of finite type, with finite-dimensional coherent cohomology vanishing in degrees ≥ 2).
Pic(X) is the group of isomorphism classes of line bundles on X itself (Tau Ceti's LineBundleClass X with its group law), not the k-points of a Picard scheme: line bundles are defined over the base.

Part (c), with δ_X the usual index over all closed points, assumes dim X = 1. When dim X = 0, X = Spec K for a finite extension K/k, Pic(X) = 0, χ_k(x) = rank(x)·[K : k], and image(rank, deg_k ∘ det) = ℤ × {0}. Part (b) always indexes CodimensionOnePoint X, an empty type in this case.
proofSteps: χ_k is additive: f_! is a homomorphism G₀(X) → G₀(Spec k) (SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.7, from additivity of the long exact cohomology sequence and finite-dimensionality of coherent cohomology on proper X, JacobianChallenge layer B), G₀(Spec k) ≅ ℤ by dimension, and c_X is additive.

(a) By KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/curve-rank-determinant-equivalence every x is (n − 1)[O_X] + [L] with n = rank x and L = det x. Hence χ_k(x) = (n − 1)χ(O_X) + χ(L) = nχ(O_X) + deg_k L by the definition of deg_k. Applying this to x = [L] + [M] − 2[O_X], whose determinant is L ⊗ M, gives deg_k(L ⊗ M) = deg_k L + deg_k M.

(b) For y of codimension one, the skyscraper κ(y)_y has H⁰ = κ(y), of k-dimension the residue degree of y, and no higher cohomology because it is flasque; in Tau Ceti main these are Scheme.finrank_cohomology_zero_skyscraperResidueField and Scheme.isFlasque_skyscraperResidueField (not at the pinned commit). So χ_k(c_X⁻¹[κ(y)_y]) = [κ(y) : k]. The class c_X⁻¹[κ(y)_y] = [O_X] − [O_X(−y)] has rank 0 and determinant O_X(y) (KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/skyscraper-class), so (a) gives deg_k O_X(y) = [κ(y) : k].

(b, continued) cl is additive in D (KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/point-class-map) and det ∘ cl sends D to the class of O_X(D); summing the point case gives χ_k(cl[D]) = deg_k O_X(D) = Σ_y n_y [κ(y) : k], which is the pinned SchemeWeilDivisor.relativeDegree f D (relativeDegree_ofPoint on generators).

(c) Assume dim X = 1, so the closed points are precisely the codimension-one points. Then rank ⊕ det is bijective onto ℤ ⊕ Pic(X), and every line bundle on X is O_X(D) for a Weil divisor D (Tau Ceti main's SchemeWeilDivisor.classGroupAddEquivLineBundleClass, owned by JacobianChallenge layer A). So deg_k(Pic X) is the image of relativeDegree f, the subgroup generated by the residue degrees of closed points, which is δ_X ℤ; a k-rational point has residue degree one.

Compatibility with SchemeAndStackFoundations §3.3: for x = [E] with E locally free of rank r, (a) reads χ(E) = r·χ(O_X) + deg_k(det E), which is §3.3's definition of vectorBundleDegree combined with its _det law (Stacks 0AYR and 0DJ5); in rank one deg_k is §3.3's vectorBundleDegree and Tau Ceti main's LineBundleClass.eulerDegree. Nothing here re-proves those statements; the node supplies their K₀ form and the comparison with the point-class map.

Dimension-zero check: a connected regular noetherian zero-dimensional scheme is Spec K for a field K, finite over k by properness. Every line bundle is trivial and there are no codimension-one points. Thus relativeDegree has zero image, (rank, deg_k ∘ det) has image ℤ × {0}, while χ_k[κ(y)] = [K : k] for its unique codimension-zero point. Its usual index [K : k] does not give the second-coordinate image.
acceptance: X = P¹_k: χ_k[O(n)] = n + 1 = 1·χ(O) + n (the §5.7 Check test_pushforward_pone); δ = 1 and (rank, deg_k ∘ det) is an isomorphism K₀(P¹_k) ≅ ℤ² (KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.6/projective-line-rank-pic).
X = P¹_ℚ and y the closed point t² + 1 = 0 of the affine chart, with κ(y) = ℚ(i): χ_ℚ(cl[y]) = 2 and O_X(y) ≅ O(2); a point-counting degree would give 1.

The conic C : x² + y² + z² = 0 over ℝ has no real point; every closed point has residue field ℂ, so δ_C = 2, χ(O_C) = 1, and (rank, deg ∘ det) : K₀(C) → ℤ² has image ℤ ⊕ 2ℤ although Pic(C) ≅ ℤ (KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.6/pointless-conic-test). A plan that took Pic to be the ℝ-points of the Picard scheme would wrongly admit a class of degree one.
An elliptic curve E over k with rational origin: χ(O_E) = 0, so χ_k(x) = deg_k(det x), and δ_E = 1; EllipticKTheory E.2 uses the origin to split the degree.

X = Spec K with [K : k] = d > 0: Pic(X) = 0, there are no codimension-one points, χ_k[O_X] = d and image(rank, deg_k ∘ det) = ℤ × {0}. It needs a canonical isomorphism det E′ ⊗ det E″ ≅ det E for every short exact sequence of finite locally free sheaves of locally constant rank (Stacks 0B38). §5.7's K0.toG0_bijective applies to non-separated schemes with the resolution property. The affine line with doubled origin has it, through the ample family {O(0′), O(0″)}, but has no ample invertible sheaf, and K₀ = G₀ = ℤ² there.
